PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 1.
FADE IN:

scenes.heading: EXT. LONGBOROUGH SCHOOL FOR BOYS - NIGHT

lines.text: Establishing. The school at night.

scenes.heading: INT. BOARDING SCHOOL - KITCHEN - NIGHT - FLASHBACK

lines.text: The haunting, lonely kitchen, illuminated by the pale light of
the moon, has a visitor: YOUNG NED. Tiptoeing in stocking feet.
At this moment, Young Ned is 9 years, 9
months, 15 days, 10 hours and 2 minutes old.
Awakened by loneliness-induced insomnia, he
found himself in desperate need of comfort.
TIME CUT. Ned, no stranger to this kitchen, has littered the
tabletops with flour, pie tins, milk and fruit. He bakes.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
And “comfort,” for Ned, meant pie. The risks
were great, but Young Ned rationalized his
rogue impulse baking as sheep-counting.
TIME CUT. Ned now has a delicious pie before him. He smiles,
cuts a big slice and happily eats.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
What harm could come of a single pie, in the
dark of night, with all the evidence ingested?
EUGENE walks in. Stops dead in his tracks. Staring.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
He was caught in flagrante delicto by one
Eugene Mulchandani...
Eugene stares at Ned. Ned stares at Eugene.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...who immediately joined him in the act.
TIME CUT. The two boys eat side-by-side, faces smeared with
filling.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Ned and Eugene were unprepared for what
happened next.
The boys stop. REVERSE TO REVEAL a BUNCH OF BOYS now standing
at the kitchen entrance. Silent. Slightly awed. Staring.
CAMERA PUSHES IN ON INGMAR TODD. He smiles, an idea forming.
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 2.
CONTINUED:
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
The aroma of freshly-baked pie, wafting
through boarding school halls, awakened an
entire class who had but one thing in common:
Ned and Eugene now sit in the middle of the GROUP of boys, all
happily eating pie, getting along, stuffing their faces.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
They were all far from home and needed
comfort. The longing and homesickness which
filled the school like a plague was magically
lifted with every bite...
Ingmar Todd stands at the door, collecting dollar bills as, one
by one, his SCHOOL CHUMS file into:
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...and the party began.
ROARING ‘20S MUSIC plays as the boys all whoop it up. They
dance, eat pie, Ned bakes more. It’s all got a SPEAKEASY,
“Flappers Gone Wild” feel to it -- until -- CLAP! A grown-up
hand slaps down hard upon young Ned’s shoulder. Music STOPS.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Until it stopped.
THE PRINCIPAL looks down upon Ned with an old man’s frown.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
And Young Ned learned that even a forkful of
immediate gratification can lead to a world of
grave consequences.
Ned, his apron removed, is marched out by the principal, past
all the other boys -- a walk of shame. His face fills frame.
MATCHING CUT: ADULT NED’s face. His expression has not changed.
A lesson to be learned again years later at
the grave of Charles Charles, currently-dead
father of the girl called Chuck.
PULL BACK to show Ned and CHUCK standing in the freshly-dug
grave of Charles Charles (RE-USE EPISODE 207, “ROBBING HOOD”).
Ready?
Chuck’s nervous, but she climbs into the grave.
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 3.
CONTINUED:
I’m ready. I think.
Ned flips the casket open. Prepares to alive-again Chuck’s
father. When:
CHUCK (CONT’D)
Wait.
What?
If we each get half a minute, you go first.
No, no. You go. If you spill over the first
thirty seconds, then no biggie. As opposed to
spilling over the second thirty seconds, which
would be yes biggie.
I’m not gonna spill. I budgeted every second.
Five seconds for “I miss you”s, ten seconds
for “I love you”s and fifteen seconds to give
him his birthday present.
That’s not enough seconds. You should have
all sixty. We don’t need to fact-find about
Dwight. I don’t know what I was thinking.
You were thinking it was important to protect
us from a mysterious, potentially-dangerous
man. You go first.
No, you go. This is awkward.
Go first or I hit you with the shovel.
A solid closing argument. Chuck nods, Ned touches the body, it
blue-SPARKS back to life. Sits up in shadow. Ned talks fast.
Hi, Mr. Charles or do I just call you Charles
doesn’t matter it’s me, Ned. I lived across
the street from you when I was a little boy.
Hi, Dad. It’s me, Charlotte. You’ve been
dead twenty years.
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 4.
CONTINUED: (2)
The SHADOWY CORPSE visibly reacts. Ned plows through, eager to
get out of the way of the father-daughter reunion.
I’m sure you have a lot of questions, but can
you put ‘em on hold for just a second and tell
us: Is Dwight Dixon a bad man?
CHARLES CHARLES, a figure SEEN ONLY IN SHADOW, answers in a
slightly-gravelly, head-cold voice:
Yes.
Oh. Uh-oh. He stole Chuck -- I still call your
daughter “Chuck,” still, like when I was nine--
Fifteen.
No, I was nine.
Seconds.
(snapping back)
Dwight stole your pocket watch and left a
veiled threat about exposing a very big secret
he knows we probably don’t want exposed.
If he got the watch, you got nothin’ to worry
about. The threat’s his insurance policy.
You don’t say nothing, he’ll return the favor.
Good to know. You’re up.
Ned gives Chuck a quick, loving look -- and goes. As he walks
away from the open grave, CAMERA TRACKS BACK with him, leaving
Chuck behind. Ned turns and watches from a distance.
The Pie-Maker’s gift of life lasted for one
precious minute only. A minute he eagerly
shared with the Chuck of his life...
REVERSE: CLOSE ON Ned, smiling, watching his good deed. DISTANT
LIGHTNING FLASHES across the sky, followed by a THUNDERCLAP.
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 5.
CONTINUED: (3)
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...to give her but half a minute to catch up
on a lifetime with a father long lost.
Ned checks his watch. And the smile is replaced with sadness.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
30 seconds were all he could give, and not a
second more.
Ned and Chuck are spooning. Yes, spooning, Chuck safely wrapped
up in boyfriend Ned’s loving arms. They are safe, however, as a
curving PLASTIC SHEET divides them. Ned is dead to the world,
lightly snoring. Chuck stares into middle-distance. Then:
Ned?
No response. He’s asleep. Chuck slowly peels his arm off and
slips out, onto the floor. She looks back, bends and kisses him
on the cheek through a corner of the plastic and leaves.
As Chuck soundlessly broke the bonds of her
plastic-wrap embrace and snuck away to beat
the break of day...

scenes.heading: INT. CHUCK’S AUNTS’ HOUSE - EARLY MORNING

lines.text: VIVIAN sits on the couch, her coat draped over her lap, waiting.
...Vivian waited for Dwight Dixon, gentleman
caller, unaware her sister Lily chased him off
their front porch 3 hours earlier.
Vivian turns to the door and waits. She looks stunning and
sexy. She waits. And waits.

scenes.heading: INT. DWIGHT’S MOTEL ROOM - EARLY MORNING

lines.text: LILY sits in Dwight’s motel room, the one stashed with weapons,
last seen in Episode 207. She calmly faces the door, shotgun on
her lap, just like Josh Brolin in “No Country for Old Men.”
Sister Lily would make certain Dwight Dixon,
gentleman caller, would never call again.
Lily bites into a saltine, keeps waiting. A shadow passes under
the doorway crack of light. Lily silently lifts the gun. The
door opens and DWIGHT DIXON walks in.
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 6.
CONTINUED:
To find Lily’s shotgun aimed right at him. He freezes.
Way I see this, we both have something you want.
What would that be, my spicy cocktail?
Lily lifts her free hand and dangles... Charles Charles’s GOLD
WATCH on its chain.
I got my daughter’s watch and you got your
insides where you want ‘em.
(then)
You’re gonna dig up Charlotte’s grave and
you’re gonna put this watch back where you
found it. After you tell me your real story.
Dwight smiles his disarming killer smile. Unseen by Lily, he
reaches around behind his back and wraps fingers around the
REVOLVER tucked in his waistband. Still charming:
Well. It all began when I was conceived in
the sweat and sawdust of a traveling carnival.
My mother was the bearded lady and my father
was an acrobat named--
Dwight whips the gun out fast, but Lily’s trigger finger is a
split-second faster and she -- BOOM!
SEEN FROM OUT IN THE HALLWAY:
Dwight and the whole motel door get BLOWN OFF, flying toward us,
revealing Lily, standing Clint Eastwood triumphant amidst the
swirling SMOKE, and we CUT TO:
LILY. Still sitting where she was, biting a saltine.
Both sisters remained ladies in waiting.
The door is on its hinges. Dwight hasn’t arrived. Lily gives
up. Grabs a pen and scrawls a note. Leaves. CAMERA HOLDS ON
THE NOTE: “I GOT IT. U WANT IT? CEMETERY. - L.”

scenes.heading: INT. PIE HOLE - DINING AREA - EARLY MORNING

lines.text: The Pie Hole is closed. Ned watches Chuck make her way across
the counter, filling sugar bottles with sugar from a pitcher.
I’m declaring it an emotional snow day.
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 7.
CONTINUED:
But you love that cook-off. And you and Olive
didn’t get to go last year.
I chose not to go last year. I was busy.
Because of me.
I like being busy because of you. And I’m
looking forward to being busy because of you
all day. You can’t just do what you did last
night and not be... overwhelmed.
I admit I’m plenty whelmed. But not overly.
Overly is on its way. Probably looking in the
window right now. You had to say hello-again
and goodbye-again to your dad in 30 seconds.
I just told myself it was thirty seconds more
than we were supposed to have.
How’d that work?
Still hurt. It didn’t matter how I budgeted
my seconds. The hello-againing was wonderful
and the goodbye-againing... wasn’t.
(then)
You should go to that cook-off.
You’re trying to get rid of me.
No, I’m not. I think I need an emotional snow
day, too.
You need an emotional snow day from me? Am I
school? Oh, no. Is it weird now? Are we
weird now because I did... it with your dad?
Not weird. I’ve never felt more in love with
you. But I’m also feeling a whole lot of
other things.
(MORE)
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 8.
CONTINUED: (2)
So many things I wanna tell you, I don’t wanna
tell you, I’m afraid to tell you, I don’t know
how to tell you.
You don’t have to tell me if you don’t want
to. I mean, you do. Eventually.
I will. Tonight. I promise. In the
meantime, Olive’s counting on you. She said
two years ago, she could taste that first
prize Blue Ribbon. Until that taste was
replaced with the bitter tang of defeat.
Bitter tang, bitter Olive. It’s a story.
This time it’s gonna have a happy ending. Go
to the cook-off. Olive will love you for it.
OFF that pronouncement...
Ned and OLIVE, dressed in brilliantly-designed outfits
representing the hometown goodness of the Pie Hole, enter the
world of the Papen County “BEST IN BELLY” COMFORT FOOD COOK-OFF,
a PAGEANT-LIKE baking contest. They pass VARIOUS CONTESTANTS,
each dressed in their respective food-based outfit, each
stationed at a Googie architecture-style station (”RINGS OF
FIRE” onion rings, “DER WAFFLE IRON,” etc.). Among them is
COLONEL LIKKIN of COLONEL LIKKIN’S SOUTHERN FRIED CHICKEN.
Isn’t it great to be back again? Just you and
me, shoulder-to-shoulder, eye-to-eye,
decorative hats fixed squarely on sweaty
brows, bonding in the fiery kiln of
competition that forges men’s souls.
We’re baking pie, Olive.
Not “pie.” Damn great pie. This is our year.
We’re in a better place than we were two years
ago. I, for one, am no longer encumbered with
the tension of a sexual nature toward you.
I’m focused. This is why coaches tell their
players to abstain before a big game. Focus.
I never really played sports.
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 9.
CONTINUED:
We should have won last time. Would’ve won,
if we hadn’t gotten screwed by...
CAMERA SWOOSHES IN on Olive, now filled with quiet, deadly rage.
OLIVE (CONT’D)
...the Buffalo.
REVERSE TO REVEAL MARIANNE MARIE BEETLE, of MUFFIN BUFFALO,
whipping up a batch of muffins and chatting up some JUDGES.
OLIVE (CONT’D)
Sweet Lord in Heaven, how I hate the Buffalo.
LEO BURNS, the obese, blinding COOK-OFF AIDE (think Julie, your
cruise director) toddles up on his Rascal.
When you say “Buffalo,” do mean the noble
breed of bison lost forever to settlers’ greed
or the upstate New York hamlet still thirsting
for Super Bowl glory?
I mean the galloping bitch on wheels whipping
up those crap muffins over there.
Marianne Marie Beetle. They call her the
Pastry Slayer. Every competitive pie, tart
and sweet quiche that crosses her path gets
gored on the horns of Muffin Buffalo.
He shakes their hands.
LEO BURNS (CONT’D)
Leo Burns, the new Comfort Food Cook-Off
Coordinator and lover of all things foody.
I just love that all foods are welcome at this
year’s Comfort Food Cook-Off.
It’s like best in show, only, “best in belly.”
Which means Buffalo Muffin will be locking
those horns with Colonel Likkin.
Leo surreptitiously points to the Colonel Sanders-like COLONEL
LIKKIN, glad-handing some fans.
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 10.
CONTINUED: (2)
LEO BURNS (CONT’D)
The Colonel will be frying himself this year.
Not “frying himself,” but he himself will be
frying. Chicken. It’s an honor to watch.
The honor will be frying his ass up extra
crispy and taking First Place.
He and the Buffalo are the teams to beat.
Likkin’s been the Best in Belly Blue Ribbon
winner fifteen years running. But there’s an
empty winner’s plate, waiting to be loaded.
(bows, points to hat)
With Damn Great Pie!
You’re the Pie Holers! I’m a very, very, very
big fan. As Event Coordinator, I’m not
allowed to say this, but I’m rooting for you.
He’s a dreamboat. Well, tugboat. But still.
Let’s set up. Partner.
As Leo toddles off on his scooter, Ned and Olive move on,
passing various booths. They pass Marianne Marie.
Don’t see her, don’t see her, not seeing her.
Ted! So nice to see you came back after
taking a year off to lick your wounds and hide
in the dank shadows of humiliating defeat.
And you were so close...
Yeah. Mysterious. As if someone deliberately
sabotaged our oven, Cheater McGee.
It’s a poor workman who blames his tools.
Just keep your oven mitts to yourself.
I plan to, as I present more award-winning
muffins to the judges. And you remember, now:
Losing doesn’t make you a loser. Oh, wait.
It does. Better get stuffing your pie holes!
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 11.
CONTINUED: (3)
Ned pulls angry Olive away.
That Buffalo is going down.
But despite the freshly-stoked heat of the
competition before him, the Pie-Maker’s
thoughts strayed away from pastries to be
made, and toward Chuck...
OMIT

scenes.heading: EXT. CHUCK’S AUNTS’ HOUSE - STREET - DAY

lines.text: Establishing.
...wondering what she could possibly be afraid
to tell him...

scenes.heading: EXT. NED’S CHILDHOOD HOME - STREET - DAY

lines.text: Establishing.
...and knowing how secrets make secret-keepers
feel lonely...
Chuck enters a darkened room. Looks scared. Crosses the room
toward a shadowy corner...
...never suspecting that Chuck was not alone
at all.
She moves quickly to a MYSTERY MAN and hugs him in an embrace:
Hi, Dad.
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 12.
CAMERA DESCENDS FROM THE HEAVENS to FIND Chuck and Ned standing
over the coffin of Charles Charles, as before.
You’re up.
Ned gives Chuck a quick, loving look -- and climbs out of the
grave. As he walks away, CAMERA TRACKS BACK with him, leaving
Chuck behind, then TRACKS BACK to Chuck, leaving Ned behind.
Hello, again. I know I don’t look like the
Charlotte you remember--
Oh, you’re the Charlotte I remember all right.
Button-button. Cute as. Now isn’t this nice.
I missed you, Dad. Sonofabitch.
(looks at watch)
Now we’re eating into our “I love you” time.
I love you and “Happy Birthday.”
It’s my birthday?
Not today, but it was gonna be.
Then I died.
I never got to give this to you. But now I
can. So I guess in a way it is your birthday.
Chuck hands her father the wallet she made for him as a child.
A LIGHTNING FLASH ARCS overhead, followed by a THUNDERCLAP. She
HUGS him tight. Then pulls back, an idea forming...
CHUCK (CONT’D)
It’s your birthday. Put on my gloves. Hurry.
She quickly pulls off her gloves and he pulls them on. She
looks over her shoulder to see Ned approaching. Chuck gives her
father one last hug and whispers in his ear:
CHUCK (CONT’D)
When he touches you, play dead. I’ll be back
to dig you up in an hour.
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 13.
CONTINUED:
What?
Chuck backs away as Ned jumps back in the grave.
I love you, Dad.
(intrigued)
I love you, too, button-button.
The Pie-Maker gave every second he could give
and not a second more.
It was nice to see you again, Mister Charles.
(intrigued and confused)
Yup. You, too, Nedly.
Torn between the Pie-Maker she loved and
the father she lost, Chuck looked for a
sign to rationalize the betrayal she was
about to commit...
Ned extends his hand, and as Charles Charles takes it, A BOLT OF
LIGHTNING FLASHES ACROSS THE SKY with an IMMEDIATE THUNDERCLAP.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...and miraculously found it.
Ned startles as Charles Charles drops back into his coffin.
Chuck blinks, startled by the timing of the lighting flash.
Are you okay?
Uh-huh.
She quickly closes the lid on her father’s coffin.
Chuck is wrapping the gauze around her seated father’s head.
The job almost complete, he looks like “The Invisible Man.”
It didn’t feel like twenty years. It felt
like something, but... Do the years you spent
being dead count as part of your lifetime?
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 14.
CONTINUED:
Best left to philosophers. What did it feel
like if it didn’t feel like twenty years?
Gliding. Holding your breath and being able
to breathe and just... gliding.
I didn’t glide.
Now, why would you have any business gliding?
I died. And then Ned touched me. But there
wasn’t any gliding, there was just... Ned.
And he never touched you again?
No. He can’t. Not without--
Good.
Chuck can’t help but smile.
CHARLES CHARLES (CONT’D)
How is this possible? You, me, here again in
the here-and-now when we belong in the
hereafter? Since when did death get a loophole?
Since Ned. Your dreams are gonna be a lot
more vivid now. It’s neat. And my bees--
You have bees?
Since you died. Then they died and Ned
touched them, too. Now their honey is...
well, you’ve never had honey like this.
Hate to look in the gift horse’s mouth, but
I’m not gonna start craving human flesh, am I?
No. Although everything does taste better.
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 15.
CONTINUED: (2)
What’s the catch, button? Hiding me away like
every stray cat, dog and goose that met your
acquaintance. You don’t want Nedly-Deadly to
know my bucket’s still kicking. Why?
(then)
Is there a catch?
Not that you’re aware of.
What?
Not that I’m aware of.
(off his look)
Okay. There’s a catch. And I have to go
catch it before I get caught.
You gonna tell me what this catch is, button?
I will. Tonight. I promise.
As Chuck’s plan was percolating...
CAMERA PULLS BACK FROM A JAPANESE COFFEE SYPHON to find EMERSON
COD sitting at his desk. The coffee syphon percolates.
...Private Investigator Emerson Cod gently
extracted the delicate flavors of Bolivia Wara
coffee grounds for a smooth, clean coffee
experience on a morning that would soon prove
to be anything but smooth or clean.
Chuck barges in:
Emerson!
Emerson holds up a “one moment” finger to her, takes a sip of
coffee from his already-poured cup, then sets it down.
CHUCK (CONT’D)
I need your help.
Pay help or friend help?
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 16.
CONTINUED:
Chuck puts her hands on her hips.
EMERSON (CONT’D)
Damn. See that? That’s the kind of body
language you never hear with pay help.
Chuck’s façade begins to crumble and continues to do so over:
Ned brought my father back to life, but only
for a minute and when the minute was up, Ned
touched him again like we always do. No
biggie. But yes biggie. In the heat of the
moment, my thinking wasn’t so much “thinking”
as “feeling.” I couldn’t help myself and I
tricked Ned with my gloves and my father’s
alive which Ned doesn’t know. Please help me.
Emerson watches. Thinks. Then:
What was the part about your gloves?
I’m a horrible person. I used Ned. My dad’s
alive because I have impulse-control issues
and now somebody else is dead.
(beat)
What do I do?
First, blow.
He hands her a box of tissues.
EMERSON (CONT’D)
Second, trust.
You’re not mad?
Furious. Steaming. Red-hot. I’ll yell at
you later, girl. Right now, I’m gonna help.
CLOSE ON a pie pan as -- PLOP! A load of berries gets loaded
in. Olive is cooking, and fast. Ned tries to help as she
blasts past him, putting the newly-made berry pie in the oven.
I don’t want your help. You’re slowing the
roll, chief. I’m in the zone.
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 17.
CONTINUED:
Ned looks across the way to see Marianne Marie matching Olive’s
every move, baking muffins, exchanging the stink-eye.
(calling out)
Working awful hard for disappointment over
there.
I am gonna win that Blue Ribbon, wrap it
around her neck and strangle her with it.
Olive. You’re baking with hate.
Rich, buttery, high-in-carbohydrate hate. You
know what no one tells you about cooking with
the Dark Side? The food is really good.
She goes back to the oven, Ned follows her, reasoning.
Revenge is a dish best served cold. We make
pie. Warm, delicious, happy-making pie.
Olive sends a cloud of flour into the air.
Help cook or get out of the kitchen, short-
pants.
Fine.
Ned helps. Marianne Marie, across the way, is one step ahead.
She pulls a tray of muffins from the oven, smells them...
Ah, the sweet smell of victory.
Not this year, turd-muffin.
I’ll shut your pie hole good.
Bring it, stale-cakes. We’re gonna win.
Who’s “we,” sucka? I’m gonna win.
They, like every CONTESTANT on the floor, STOP COLD when they
hear a blood-curdling SCREAM!
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 18.
CONTINUED: (2)
Leo Burns rides his Rascal at top speed to the source of the
screaming, to Colonel Likkin’s closed-curtained cooking station.
He pulls the curtain back as the chefs crowd around him to see:
The Colonel is halfway in his own boiling vat of grease. His
wife and sous-chef, THE WIDOW LIKKIN, is screaming.
My husband, the Colonel! He’s dead!
Ned rushes forward and, using OVEN MITTS, PULLS the Colonel from
his own bubbling vat. The man is a deep-fried CORPSE.
Not just dead. He’s extra crispy.
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 19.
Ned, Olive, Marianne Marie, Leo and other chef contestants look
on, sadly, as distraught sous-chef, the Widow Likkin, rambles
in shock.
My husband, the Colonel, gone forever.
I’m afraid it looks like he collapsed and fell
into his own boiling oil.
I always knew one of his many massive heart
attacks would do him in -- no man in his prime
should collapse into his own deep fryer, it’s
just so undignified...
True. At least the Colonel left this world
fryin’.
Should be some comfort.
There’s no comfort knowing the secret recipe
will die along with him. The recipe was the
Colonel’s life’s work, his greatest and only
legacy.
Surely he wrote it down.
Surely he didn’t. My husband was a fat-frying
savant. Kept the recipe stored in his head.
Worth a fortune, built his franchise on one
deep, original taste. If only I could have
him back, for one minute -- to preserve his
lasting, loving memory.
She SOBS. Ned frowns, then eyes the PARAMEDICS, who are
preparing to enter the curtained-off cooking station. Knows
what he must do.
Olive. I need you. Help me help the widow.
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 20.
CONTINUED:
How? Her husband’s dead, what are you gonna
do? Haul him back to life and say, “Dude,
what’s your recipe?”
Pause.
Maybe he left something behind. Just distract
the paramedics long enough for me to, uh,
examine his workstation.
He ducks behind the curtain. As the paramedics almost pass,
Olive sticks her fingers in a bowl of raspberry sauce, smears it
on her face:
Ahh! My eyes are bleeding!
She runs away. The paramedics follow.
Ned steps in and shuts the curtain. He’s ALONE with the extra-
crispy corpse of the Colonel and -- SPARK! -- un-deads him.
I finally know what my birds felt like.
(re: himself)
Guess I’m dead, eh?
Heart attack. Not a lot of time and the Widow
Likkin wants to preserve your secret recipe.
Good woman, my bride. Let’s do it. I got all
500 herbs and spices right up here. Better
pull up a chair and grab a pen.
That sounds like a long trip down a lazy river
we don’t have time for.
You can’t rush goodness.
(then)
Did you say, “Heart attack”?
(grabbing pen and pad)
I did. Shall we start with herbs or spices?
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 21.
CONTINUED:
Bushwah! Some carpetbagging coward snuck up
behind, battered me in my own batter and shoved
me into boiling oil. It was murder, son.
(this is news)
Really? But you didn’t see who did it?
Attacked from behind. They were stealthy,
like a snake or a Yankee.
(nervously checks his watch)
Okay, why don’t we hit the headlines of the
recipe and then with the time left over we
can circle back around to the murder -- this
is silly. Are you sure you didn’t write the
recipe down?
I did.
You did? And we couldn’t have just started
with that?
Don’t usually trust fast-talkers. Got one
handwritten copy. Keep it right here in my...
The Colonel reaches for his breast pocket. But his arm, deep-
fried, crackles and will not bend. Crispy bits break off.
COLONEL LIKKIN (CONT’D)
Here in my... tarnation, the fat-frying
process seems to have robbed me of mobility.
Ned takes a set of tongs from nearby and, with a nod of
permission, digs into the Colonel’s breast pocket. Empty.
There’s nothing there.
Impossible! I’ve kept my recipe right there --
the same spot for thirty years. What
scoundrel stole my secret recipe?
I’ll find out. And I’ll find out who killed
you, too. But now, I’m afraid time is up.
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 22.
CONTINUED: (2)
I hate to go. But at least I’m going delicious.
Ned shivers, grossed-out and touches the Colonel, RE-DEADING him
just as the curtains part, the PARAMEDICS wheel their gurney in.
And as the Colonel went back to being dead...
Emerson is shrugging on his coat as Chuck leads him to the door.
...Chuck faced the consequences of her impulsive
decision to bring her father back to life.
The bring-Dad-back part I don’t regret. How
can you regret reuniting with someone you love
who you thought you’d never see again?
Point taken.
The much bigger problem -- maybe the biggest
problem, in an objective sense -- is the
dishonesty with Ned and the making-someone-
else-less-alive part.
“Less alive.” Nice euphemism, killer.
We were at the cemetery in the dead of night.
There was nobody else was around. Maybe
nobody died.
You think this is a “sometimes” rule? Ned
lets a person stay alive longer than a minute
and someone else has to die sometimes? No.
It’s an “every time” rule and some sucker’s
dead in the leaves.
Chuck rises, agitated.
Oh, god. I may have killed some nice old lady
with insomnia who was taking flowers to her
husband. Or an old-time grounds keeper whom
everyone loves and calls “Pops”? Or...
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 23.
CONTINUED:
Either way, there’s a dead body to find.
Which was deaded by Ned, only he don’t know
about it on account of you didn’t tell him.
And that’s the wrong I’m correcting.
I know what I did was wrong -- but I was
spurred to action by the spur-of-the-moment
which leaves me living in the deep, dark world
of consequence. But if you help me clean this
up, then Ned won’t have to live anywhere but
the bright, happy world of pie. And then all
Ned and I will have to deal with is each other.
And your daddy. You can’t keep that from him.
(then, off her, relenting)
Okay. We take care of the body first, but
then you go straight to Pie Boy.
(beat)
You ain’t gonna start bawling again, are you?
Chuck gratefully kisses him on the cheek.
Thank you.
Don’t be pecking me, woman! That’s the peck
of cahoots, which we are definitely not in.
Thank you anyway.
PRE-LAP:
THE WIDOW LIKKIN (V.O.)
The cook-off will continue.
In front of the cordoned-off workstation for Colonel Likkin.
Leo Burns stands by the widow as she addresses the ASSEMBLED
CHEFS, Ned, Olive and Marianne Marie included.
The Colonel would have wanted it that way.
His tragic heart attack must be honored by us,
his sacred community of fellow chefs.
They all bow their heads a beat. Then:
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 24.
CONTINUED:
Who now all stand a much better chance of
winning. Proceed.
They BOLT back to their cooking stations. We favor Ned and Olive.
It’s a tragedy, obviously, but you know what
they say -- when God closes a door, he opens
an oven.
“They” don’t say that. Or if they do, they
don’t have much compassion for a dead Colonel.
I’m not going to let you bait me into getting
all soft and compassiony when we’re this close
to nailing this competition.
What would you say if I told you I think the
Colonel was murdered?
Boohoo, more room at the top.
(then)
See? I am in the zone.
(then, off him)
Oh my God, you’re not kidding.
I think the Colonel had a copy of his secret
recipe and someone killed him for it.
How could you possibly know that from looking
at his dead body?
(vamping)
I... am an investigator. Working alongside
Emerson has taught me things. Deductive and
inductive reasoning, evidence gathering. Dead
bodies have a lot to say... to the trained
professional.
Uh-huh.
And anyway, my educated hunch says there’s a
murder to solve.
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 25.
CONTINUED: (2)
Does your hunch realize you don’t have Emerson
or Chuck to help you? You’ve never solved a
murder mystery alone before.
I’m not alone.
Me? Ooh. I just got all tingly, and not just
in the nether regions. How do we do it, the
whole P.I. thing? Sneak around all cloak-and-
dagger, or do we just jam a gun in the
suspect’s mouth and say, “Sing, canary, before
I decorate this wallpaper with your guts”?
Neither. And technically, I don’t believe you
can blow someone’s guts out their mouth.
Wuss.
They reach their own cooking station. Olive slides back the
curtain to REVEAL -- their pies have been SABOTAGED. Filling is
slopped all over the place, flour everywhere and the oven SMOKES.
OLIVE (CONT’D)
Holy smokes, our oven’s smoking!
Olive puts on oven mitts and rips open the oven door. Pulls a
tray out, littered with burnt, smoking hockey pucks of pies.
OLIVE (CONT’D)
Sabotaged. I’ll bet it was the Beetle.
And I bet it was the Colonel’s killer.
Chuck and Emerson walk through the cemetery together.
This doesn’t take the sting of responsibility
out altogether, but I brought cash. When we
find the body, we’ll take it to the nearest
funeral home, with cash and a note saying,
“Every human body has dignity, please bury
this one.” It’ll be just like leaving a baby
on a doorstep, only on the tail end of things.
And the point of this would be say-what?
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 26.
CONTINUED:
Closure.
Emerson stares into the bushes between two small mausoleums.
Mmm-hmm. Something tells me the body we find
will give you anything except “closure.”
Where’d you get that idea?
Oh, I didn’t get it. It was given to me.
Chuck pushes aside some shrubbery, looks, too.
By Dwight Dixon.
We see what they’re looking at: DWIGHT DIXON lies dead, a grin
on his face, slumped against a wall.
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 27.
Chuck and Emerson stand over the body of Dwight. Emerson
silent, somber. Chuck upset.
I killed him!
Bet you’re wishing you offed that sweet old
imaginary lady now.
What was Dwight Dixon doing here?
Got one theory. Looky here.
Emerson guides Chuck to show her:
ANGLE -- a partially-hidden RIFLE with a scope on a TRIPOD.
A rifle?
Emerson bends and carefully looks through the scope--
Seems like sweet ol’ Dwight was already set up
for a shot. Your weighty conscience might be
a little less weighty after you take a look.
Chuck bends to take a look.
Why would Dwight have a gun?
(then)
Hells bells...
CHUCK’S POV: Through a long lens at her father’s grave, 100
yards off.
CHUCK (CONT’D)
That’s my father’s grave. Was he going to
kill us?
Not if you killed him first.
Why would Dwight want us dead?
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 28.
CONTINUED:
As is traditional, the “why” in this case was
met with an equal and opposite “because.”

scenes.heading: INT. MOTEL ROOM - NIGHT - FLASHBACK (RE-USE FROM “ROBBING HOOD”)

lines.text: Dwight enters his motel room to discover the watch he stole from
Chuck, as well as his own, is missing. He reacts.
Upon discovering that the pocket watch he had
stolen from Chuck had been stolen back...
Lily stands still on the ledge as Dwight grabs a GUN, goes.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...Dwight set out to reclaim the mysterious
timepiece one last time.
OMIT
Dwight assembles his rifle...
Following Chuck to the graveyard, Dwight
assumed her intent was to return the watch to
the grave from which it had been stolen.
Dwight squints through the scope, looking across the graveyard.
DWIGHT’S POV: THROUGH THE SCOPE CROSSHAIRS.
Ned and Chuck flip open Charles Charles’s casket.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Ready to pull the trigger and reclaim his
prize, Dwight paused, unbelieving the
unbelievable sight he saw.
A blue spark FLASH lights Ned’s and Chuck’s features as a
shadowy figure of the dead rises from the grave.
DWIGHT -- pulls back from the scope, then looks again...
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Dwight’s mind reeled at the miraculous event
before him, and, as is traditional, he
decided to put an end to the thing he did
not understand.
CLOSE ON HIS TRIGGER FINGER, preparing to squeeze...
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 29.
CONTINUED:
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
But, as all his reeling and unbelieving had
taken exactly 61 seconds...
Dwight DROPS DEAD, OUT OF FRAME.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...no shot was ever fired.
CLOSE ON Dwight’s FACE as he is dragged through the grass.
Chuck, dragging the body with Emerson, seems much happier.
If I hadn’t kept my father alive, I’d have
been murdered a second time.
Once was plenty.
And Ned would be gone, too. That’s three
points lighting up our side of the cosmic
scoreboard by getting rid of Dwight.
You saved that bundle you were gonna blow on
getting Mr. Boom-Boom buried, too. Better to
bury him here.
They arrive at Charles Charles’s grave.
EMERSON (CONT’D)
You stay here, I’ll get a shovel. We’ll get
him under the grass before the pay-your-
respects-at-lunch crowd shows up. By the time
the grass grows back on the plot, it’ll be
like none of this ever happened.
Emerson goes. Chuck waits.
I can’t wait for it to be like none of this
ever happened.
Dwight’s EYES suddenly POP OPEN:
But it did happen.
OFF Chuck, displeased and puzzled...
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 30.
Olive scrapes off the last burnt husk of a pie from her hopeless
tray of all-burnt pies as Ned examines the oven.
Someone tampered with the oven. Now the flame
won’t shut off.
Let it burn. Maybe it’ll destroy this
building and all its memories of almost
winning with the cleansing power of flame.
Olive -- we’re staying in the contest.
Olive has an instant attitude adjustment.
We are?
We need keep competing as a cover, so we can
investigate Colonel Likkin’s murder.
Winning would make an excellent cover.
Whoever killed the Colonel is a risk-taker.
Desperate. Same as our saboteur.
So find the saboteur, we find our killer.
And maybe we find our ingredients. They took
everything we need to bake pies.
I’m on it.
Olive turns to exit and stops, nearly colliding with Vivian.
Standing, dressed to the nines, makeup running. Near tears.
Olive?
Vivian?
Vivian?
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 31.
CONTINUED:
What are you doing here? Oh, honey. Are
you crying?
I stopped by the Pie Hole, but it was closed.
And, yes, I was crying.
Why’s the Pie Hole closed?
(to Vivian)
It’s man trouble, I can tell. I knew that
Dwight Dixon was heartbreak waiting to pop.
I don’t blame Dwight. And I don’t blame
myself, this time. This is Lily’s fault. She
aimed a shotgun at his privates and told him
to stay away from us. But half of us is me,
and I don’t want him away. I want him close.
(to Ned)
Give us a minute.
I’ll get back to fixing this. Good to see
you, Vivian.
Olive leads Vivian away from Ned, who returns to the oven.
Forgive me. I’m so wrapped up in finding my
man, I’m thoughtlessly keeping you from yours.
Who? Ned? No. We’re partners in a contest.
Unromantic partners. Like a brother and
sister. Like an androgenous, asexual brother
and sister. My man? Ha. Ha-ha. Ha, ha hee
ha ho. That’s a laugh.
When Dwight didn’t show up for our date, I
tried to laugh, too. Tried to tell myself my
feelings for him were silly. But lying to
yourself about love never works.
Damn.
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 32.
CONTINUED: (2)
I know. But still, I keep lying and looking all
the same. If you see Dwight at the Pie Hole,
will you tell him about the looking part? I’d
like to see him.
I understand.
Vivian exits. Olive looks back at Ned at their oven.
OLIVE (CONT’D)
Boy, do I understand.
She goes back to Ned.
Olive hoped the Pie-Maker would not find any
clues on her face that the dam around her
heart was starting to crack.
I’ve found something.
(beat)
When our saboteur sabotaged our oven, he made
one sticky mistake.
Ned puts his finger in a sticky, brown residue inside the oven.
What is it? Toxic soot with a dash of DNA?
It’s sweet. Woodsy. Like a forest in the
Berkshires in the crisp autumn dawn.
(tasting)
Caramelized sugar.
Maple syrup.
Only one chef here uses pure maple syrup.
The Waffle Nazi. The Waffle Nazi.
CAMERA WHIPS ACROSS THE COOK-OFF FLOOR TO REVEAL: Der Waffle Iron.
A Googie architecture waffle pan of a booth. Inside, the
lederhosen-clad WAFFLE NAZI berates his lederhosen-clad
ASSISTANT -- holding a waffle in her face.
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 33.
CONTINUED: (3)
You vill taste ze magic!
Ned and Olive nod knowingly. Olive weighs the spatula in her
hand, ass-kicking on her mind...
OMIT
Chuck nervously looks around for Emerson to return, but he’s not
back yet. Staring at her from the grass is the silent corpse of
Dwight Dixon. Chuck stares back, “Not afraid of you, fucker.”
Chuck had seen dead bodies talk before, but
this was different. This was just her guilty
mind giving rise to her guilty feelings.
You’re just my guilty mind giving rise to my
guilty feelings.
Dwight bursts out, merrily:
Doesn’t change the fact that you have royally
screwed up.
Fine. You talk. I’ll shovel.
Was it worth it? Sure, fine, I’m a bad man,
you saved three good people putting me down.
Three-for-one sale on the grandest scale.
Chuck looks back, anxiously. Still no Emerson...
(calling)
Anytime with those shovels!
(to Dwight)
What would you have done?
Same thing, probably. I’d have killed you,
too. But here’s the difference...
Emerson!
I would have told Ned by now.
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 34.
CONTINUED:
Shut up!
Emerson appears, carrying two shovels.
Who you talking to?
Shut up. Nothing. No one. I don’t need to
talk to anyone about anything because my
conscience is clear.
Great. Then grab a shovel.
They start shoveling. ON DWIGHT, as a shovelful of dirt lands
on his face.
Ned will never forgive you!
Chuck shovels faster.

scenes.heading: INT. COOK-OFF - DER WAFFLE IRON BOOTH - DAY

lines.text: We see Der Waffle Iron booth -- empty. Until Olive pokes her
head over the counter. Ned joins her, they sneak in.
This is an incredible violation of the
P.C.C.F.C.O. rule that no chef is allowed in
another chef’s kitchen. It’s immediate
disqualification.
Concentrate on the killer. The Waffle Nazi is
likely our saboteur.
Find the saboteur, find the killer.
Any evidence linking Waffle Nazi to Colonel
Likkin would tie up this case in brown paper,
wrapped with strong, sturdy twine.
They investigate. As they look for clues:
Know what I love about Vivian? Her imagination.
Ned, not listening, stares at THREE BOWLS of batter.
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 35.
CONTINUED:
OLIVE (CONT’D)
She thought you and I were a couple. So
crazy, it’s like imagining us as Hobbits, or
on jet packs.
Ned stirs all three batter bowls. One is slightly thicker,
harder to stir. This one interests him.
OLIVE (CONT’D)
Or Hobbits on jet packs. Isn’t the idea of us
romantically entwined a panic, a scream, a four-
hour heart attack of complete impossibility?
Ned dips his finger in, tastes the thicker mixture. Smiles.
It all makes sense.
It does?
This batter is better than batter. It’s
evidence we can use to wrap up this case.
(crushed)
Hurray. What is it?
Ned spoons Olive a taste of the batter.
OLIVE (CONT’D)
Delicious. Savory, not sweet. Bursting with
what’s gotta be, like, 500 herbs and spices.
The Colonel’s secret recipe.
Just then -- the curtain RIPS aside and the Waffle Nazi, backed
up by Marianne Marie Beetle, stands accusatorily.
And, the killer on a plate.
Sir, I accuse you of--
Sabotage!
CAMERA WHIPS to the Waffle Nazi’s own row of waffle irons. Each
and every one of them with its CORD SEVERED.
WAFFLE NAZI (CONT’D)
You haff sabotaged mein irons!
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 36.
CONTINUED: (2)
We didn’t do that.
Don’t cry, mein Herr. Look.
(checks her watch)
It’s Justice O'clock. I’m telling.
The Waffle Nazi and Marianne Marie stand together, Ned and Olive
looking guilty as sin. Busted.
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 37.
OMIT

scenes.heading: INT. COOK-OFF - DER WAFFLE IRON BOOTH - DAY

lines.text: Ned lifts up the cut waffle cord to inspect it. This only makes
him look guilty. Waffle Nazi and Marianne Marie stand blocking
the exit.
Well, Pie Holers, it looks as if you are soon
to be eliminated from the competition.
We’re kicking you out before you baked
yourself out.
When Leo Burns toodles up on his scooter and
sees how many rules you have broken, your
dreams of comfort food glory are kaput.
We’re not the saboteurs.
Oh, yah, my vaffle cord just leaped in your
arms like a puppy vanting love, zen cut itself
in two.
You saw our oven; we were sabotaged, too.
Liars roast in Hell -- just sayin’.
You sabotaged yourselves to avoid suspicion.
When we present the evidence we got, you can
kiss the cook-off auf Wiedersehen.
Long pause. The Waffle Nazi has no idea what was just said.
OLIVE (CONT’D)
It’s “goodbye” in German.
I do not speak a vord of German. I speak
English mit a German accent. Pageantry.
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 38.
CONTINUED:
We found this batch of the Colonel’s recipe in
your kitchen.
That’s a big bowl of motive, Fritz.
Motive for what? Are you suggesting murder?
Phht. Ridiculous. Herr Likkin and I were
soon to become business partners.
Chicken and waffles?
Would have caught Popeyes with their pants
down. And I have the paperwork right here.
He holds out a folder, then snatches it back as Leo arrives on
his scooter. Looks about, aghast.
What in the name of Julia Child are you people
doing? I can’t count the number of rules
violations going on here. I am so disappointed.
There may be the appearance of rules being
bent or broken completely, buy there’s a
bigger picture here you need to see.
(beat)
I just haven’t finished painting it yet.
We’re not the saboteurs.
Poppycock. The Pie Hole is disqualified.
OFF Olive’s stunned disbelief...
Chuck and Emerson finish burying Dwight.
That’ll work, let’s get out of here.
Wait. We need a priest, or a rabbi, or a
somebody to say some words. Dwight was not
the nicest person, but still every body
deserves to be buried with dignity.
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 39.
CONTINUED:
I got buttloads of dignity to sprinkle the
ground with. Get holy.
Emerson bows his head, Chuck joins him. He intones:
EMERSON (CONT’D)
Here lies Dwight, here lies his gun. He was
bad, but now he’s done. Let’s go.
They do. Chuck sighs:
All this and I still have to deal with my
mother.
You mean your father.
He looks to see Chuck is gone. Like the Dark Knight.
CHUCK (O.S.)
I mean my mother.
Emerson stops short at encountering: Lily. She’s tastefully
dressed and carries a shotgun.
Lily. Delighted.
Can the crap and sell it to tourists. What
are you doing here, Cod?
Do you care?
Not really.
ANGLE ON Chuck, hiding, but relishing Lily’s voice all the same.
Emerson gestures “get behind me” as he talks to Lily...
And might I inquire, what are you doing here?
Waiting for Dwight Dixon.
He may disappoint. Men do that.
Emerson maneuvers to keep Chuck hidden from Lily.
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 40.
CONTINUED: (2)
EMERSON (CONT’D)
And the shotgun?
Military salute.
For Dwight Dixon.
For Charles. But if I happen to miss and blow
Dwight’s head off, completely by accident,
that’s something my lawyers can pretty much
straighten out later.
Lily goes.
So lovely catching up.
Emerson looks back to Chuck, both sigh in relief.
Olive packs up her pots and pans -- dejected but resigned.
That’s everything. But there’s no bag big
enough to carry home my busted dreams of Blue
Ribbon victory.
Back to the Pie Hole. Which is closed, which
is strange, because Chuck should be there.
POV: Colonel Likkin’s booth is unoccupied and unwatched.
NED (CONT’D)
The Colonel’s chicken booth.
An empty nest -- chock-full of clues.
A really bold detective team would sneak in
for one last bit of recon before packing in
their pots and pans for good.
Olive nods. She’s in. They pack up supplies, walking out...
then DUCK INTO the Colonel’s booth while no one’s looking.

scenes.heading: INT. COOK-OFF - COLONEL LIKKIN’S BOOTH - DAY

lines.text: The place is a mess with batter mix and flour coating the floor.
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 41.
CONTINUED:
Memorize the scene -- every detail. The
prints in the batter. The footprints, gurney
tracks, the... What’s that?
Olive dabs a finger into the flour and finds, coated,
underneath, one of several bright bits of plastic.
Sprinkles! I love sprinkles. You love clues,
two great tastes that taste great together.
Olive tastes it, spits it out, appalled.
OLIVE (CONT’D)
Peeah! How come you do the detective taste-
test and get crème brûlée and I get...
They examine the shiny bits on the ground together.
Painted plastic. Cheap jewelry.
Left here before the Colonel was killed.
Which means they belong to the killer.
Engrossed in the mysterious clue before them, neither Ned nor
Olive see the MYSTERIOUS FIGURE sneak up behind them, holding a
PAN in each hand, rising them up like two deadly weapons and...
Seen outside the Colonel’s booth. We hear BONG! BONG! Beat.
Marianne Marie comes out alone. Holding two pans. Wearing two
earrings. One intact, one a little smashed, but both the color
of painted plastic -- THE COLOR OF SPRINKLES. La-di-da...
PUSHING DAISIES #208 "Comfort Food" 09/12/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 42.
CLOSE UP ON Ned and Olive, face-to-face, like lovers, so close
they’re nearly kissing.
The most important thing is to keep our wits
about us and our nerves steady.
Camera begins TILTING SIDEWAYS as Olive talks.
OLIVE (CONT’D)
There’s no good in freaking out, so don’t go
crazy and start, I dunno, kissing me or
something ridiculous like that.
CAMERA COMPLETES ITS TILT TO REVEAL Ned and Olive are, in fact,
lying together in a trunk -- Ned on top.
OLIVE (CONT’D)
Just ‘cause we’re locked in a trunk and could
die any minute.
Ned begins to push up with his back and GRUNT a bit.
OLIVE (CONT’D)
What’re you -- Hey -- clean thoughts, chum.
Ned gives one last push and pushes the lid off the trunk.

scenes.heading: INT. COOK-OFF - COLONEL LIKKIN’S BOOTH - DAY

lines.text: The trunk opens, knocking off Marianne Marie, who was sitting on
top. She holds her pans in a defensive posture as Ned and Olive
scramble out of the trunk.
You’re tangling with Muffy the Pastry Slayer.
You’re the killer!
